points.problem: request owner serial and rundown state
points.evidence: Six original async database producers allocate one context per native request. Native WSAStartup occurs once for the entire WOW process;WWS32TaskCleanup closes task sockets without native WSACleanup or async-context retirement. The original context has no task owner,so it cannot select only the exiting task requests or reject stale completion before guest buffer conversion. The existing thread serial is reused,not a new identity namespace. HWND lifetime alone cannot protect the conversion that precedes PostMessage.

Original WWS32WSACancelAsyncRequest always returns WSAEINVAL and never calls native cancellation. Native cancellation needs AsyncTaskHandle32 but guest receives AsyncTaskHandle16;the existing context list provides that mapping. Lookup borrows only the native value across the provider call;removal re-finds by task/guest handle after success to avoid keeping a context pointer across concurrent completion. Task cleanup in wsext.c calls the third helper. Removing these declarations while preserving the proved capability loses the checked BOOL/pointer/VOID signatures;restoring the original whole call chain instead removes cancellation and per-task retirement. Moving the same declarations to wsdata.c adds equal complexity elsewhere and does not restore original behavior.
